column2: bpf: Add bpf programmable net device

column1: This work adds a new
column2: minimal BPF-programmable device called ""netkit""

column1: (former PoC code-name ""meta"") we recently presented at LSF/MM/BPF. The
core idea is that BPF programs are executed within the drivers xmit routine
and therefore e.g. in case of containers/Pods moving BPF processing closer
to the source.
One of the goals was that in case of Pod egress traffic
column2: this allows to

column1: move BPF programs from hostns tcx ingress into the device itself
column2: providing

column1: earlier drop or forward mechanisms
column2: for example

column1: determines that the skb must be sent out of the node
column2: then a redirect to

column1: the physical device can take place directly without going through per-CPU
backlog queue. This helps to shift processing for such traffic from softirq
to process context
column2: leading to better scheduling decisions/performance (see

column1: measurements in the slides).
In this initial version
column2: the netkit device ships as a pair

column1: extend this further so it can also operate in single device mode. The pair
comes with a primary and a peer device. Only the primary device
column2: typically

column1: residing in hostns
column2: can manage BPF programs for itself and its peer. The

column1: peer device is designated for containers/Pods and cannot attach/detach
BPF programs. Upon the device creation
column2: the user can set the default policy

column1: to 'pass' or 'drop' for the case when no BPF program is attached.
Additionally
column2: the device can be operated in L3 (default) or L2 mode. The

column1: management of BPF programs is done via bpf_mprog
column2: so that multi-attach is

column1: supported right from the beginning with similar API and dependency controls
as tcx. For details on the latter see commit 053c8e1f235d (""bpf: Add generic
attach/detach/query API for multi-progs""). tc BPF compatibility is provided
so that existing programs can be easily migrated.
Going forward
column2: we plan to use netkit devices in Cilium as the main device

column1: type for connecting Pods. They will be operated in L3 mode in order to
simplify a Pod's neighbor management and the peer will operate in default
drop mode
column2: so that no traffic is leaving between the time when a Pod is

column1: brought up by the CNI plugin and programs attached by the agent.
Additionally
column2: the programs we attach via tcx on the physical devices are

column1: using bpf_redirect_peer() for inbound traffic into netkit device
column2: hence the

column1: latter is also supporting the ndo_get_peer_dev callback. Similarly
column2: we use

column1: bpf_redirect_neigh() for the way out
column2: pushing from netkit peer to phys device

column1: directly. Also
column2: BIG TCP is supported on netkit device. For the follow-up

column1: work in single device mode
column2: we plan to convert Cilium's cilium_host/_net

column1: devices into a single one.
An extensive test suite for checking device operations and the BPF program
and link management API comes as BPF selftests in this series.
